references.text: The Lord walks in the midst of his people, a theme that emphasizes God's presence in the camp and the need for holiness.
God's promise to go with his people and give them rest, parallel to his presence in the camp.
Israel is to be a holy people for the Lord, reflecting the requirement that the camp must be holy.
The command to be holy because the Lord is holy, which explains why the camp must be clean.
God's dwelling shall be in the midst of the people, an eschatological promise built on God's presence in the camp.
Paul quotes the promise that God will dwell and walk among his people, calling for purity and holiness.
God's dwelling among humanity in the new Jerusalem, a fulfillment of the promise of his presence.
The call to be holy in all conduct because God is holy, reflecting the requirement of a holy camp.
The Lord is a great and awesome God in the midst of the people, who delivers their enemies into their hands.
The Lord goes with the people to fight against their enemies and grant victory, parallel to the promise of deliverance.
